items.title: Gurugram: Man arrested for killing business partner, burying body in water tank
points: A 21-year-old man was arrested on Thursday for murdering his 25-year-old business partner over a financial dispute and burying his body near an abandoned water tank in Gurugram’s Sector 63A, police said.
The accused allegedly stabbed the victim and strangled him with a cotton scarf before burying the body and covering it with soil.
The accused, identified as Bablu, a resident of Badaun district in Uttar Pradesh, was arrested from his native village with four days of police custody, officials said on Friday.
According to police, the victim, Naim, who sold peanuts in Gurugram, went missing on November 8.
His brother filed a complaint at Sector 65 police station on November 11 after he failed to return home.
On November 22, they recovered a body buried near an old water tank in vacant fields close to Kadarpur T-point in Sector 63A.
The body was later identified as Naim’s, and murder charges were added to the case.

items.title: Japan Bank Shares Risk Further Unwind as Funding Cost Bites
points: Japanese banking shares face increasing risk of an unwind as higher interest rates provide less of a boost to profits amid intensifying competition across the sector.
Lenders, who have been among the biggest beneficiaries of the Bank of Japan’s shift away from ultra-low interest rates, are facing a new challenge: slowing deposit growth.
Deposit growth at banks slowed to 1.4% in October, the weakest pace in eight months, according to BOJ data.
The slowdown has been particularly pronounced at regional banks, where deposits grew only around 0.9% from a year earlier over the past three months, the slowest pace in roughly two decades.
Bank shares have already fallen around 17% from their Sept.
Before the recent pullback, bank shares had risen about 400% over the previous four years.

items.title: Dollar lingers near 22-month peak as AI worries simmer

items.title: AI Risk Sets Dollar for Longest Winning Run Since 2024
points: (Bloomberg) -- The dollar is poised for its longest monthly winning streak in two years as a rupture in the artificial intelligence trade and rising interest rates spur demand for safe-haven assets.

The greenback has strengthened against all of its Group-of-10 peers, including the Japanese yen and the Swiss franc.

items.title: Greek-Owned Fleet Retains Global Lead, While Greek Flag Remains Outside the Top Five
points: China ranked second, with a 15.0 per cent share of global capacity, followed by Japan (9.7 per cent), Singapore (7.3 per cent) and Hong Kong, China (4.9 per cent).

The UNCTAD figures, referring to 1 January 2026, show that Greece’s fleet remains substantially larger in terms of carrying capacity than those of its closest competitors.
The Greek-owned fleet comprises 5,168 vessels, of which 4,606 are registered under foreign flags and just 553 under the Greek flag.
Consequently, 88.3 per cent of Greek-owned shipping capacity is registered outside Greece, reflecting the international character of the country’s shipping industry.
The leading flag States were Liberia, Panama and the Marshall Islands, which together accounted for 44.1 per cent of global shipping capacity.
The Greek flag, by comparison, had 1,170 vessels, representing 1.0 per cent of the global fleet by vessel count, and 2.0 per cent by carrying capacity.

items.title: Tanker Shipping Market Overview & Outlook: Disruptions still dominate tanker market outlook
points: Since the start of the third quarter, however, ship-to-ship transfers in the Gulf of Oman from shuttles crossing the Strait of Hormuz have increased significantly.
Over the past four weeks, Middle East tanker exports have reached 75% of pre-war levels, even though Saudi Arabian Red Sea exports have fallen since the Houthi blockade began.
Russian clean-product exports have meanwhile averaged 58% below last year’s level since the start of the third quarter, because of Ukrainian attacks on refineries.
For 2027 and 2028, two scenarios are presented: “SoH closed” and “SoH open”.
They differ in how three situations develop: the Strait of Hormuz, the threat to Saudi Arabian Red Sea exports and the attacks affecting Russian exports.
“SoH closed” assumes that these disruptions stay unchanged, while “SoH open” assumes that all three are resolved gradually during 2027.

items.title: Baltic Dry Index Up for 4th Day
points: The Baltic Exchange’s dry bulk freight index, which tracks rates for ships carrying dry bulk commodities, advanced for a fourth straight session on Thursday, rising by 1.5% to its highest level since September 29 at 3,152 points.
The gains reflect tighter vessel availability and stronger demand for shipping capacity, particularly for capesize vessels, with rates in this segment climbing nearly 13% over the week.
Higher iron ore shipments from Australia and Brazil to China, alongside seasonal restocking ahead of winter, have supported cargo demand.
Guinea has also contributed to the increase, with rising bauxite exports and growing iron ore shipments following the ramp-up of the Simandou project.
Meanwhile, the panamax index, which usually carries 60,000 to 70,000 tons of coal or grain, rose by 2.2% to its highest since October 19 at 2,273 points.

During the hearing, Justice Pardiwala remarked, "The battle begins now." The legal battle centers on the constitution and control of the RK Family Trust and the assets transferred into it.

Sunjay Kapur's mother Rani Kapur, 81, has challenged the trust's formation, alleging that her late son and his wife Priya Sachdev Kapur transferred her assets into the trust without her informed consent, a claim disputed by the other side.

During the hearing, senior advocate Mukul Rohatgi, appearing for Priya Sachdev Kapur, told the SC that the late businessman's mother had walked out of the mediation and was now blaming her daughter-in-law, Priya, for the failure of the settlement process.
Senior Advocate Mahesh Jethmalani also appeared in the matter on behalf of Samaira and Kiaan Kapur, the children of Sunjay Kapur and actor Karisma Kapoor.

items.title: Driven out of forests, 56 displaced elephants run into politics in Karnataka
points: The movement of 56 elephants out of Hassan’s coffee estates in Karnataka has run into a political roadblock, with the forest department temporarily suspending the operation after protests by legislators and residents in neighbouring Chikkamagaluru.
The herd, meanwhile, has scattered across three districts, with 39 elephants in Mudigere, 13 back in Belur and four tuskers moving towards Kodagu as of November 26.
The operation, launched after two people were killed in elephant attacks in Belur, began on November 21, following the capture of two tuskers on November 18 and 19.
One was shifted to the Mathigodu elephant camp in Nagarahole Tiger Reserve, while the other was released into the wild in Bandipur after being fitted with a radio collar.
The forest department then began guiding the remaining 56 elephants from Belur towards the Bhadra forests.

Motamma, who represents Mudigere, submitted her resignation to the Assembly speaker on November 23, protesting against the movement of elephants into her constituency without consulting local elected representatives.

Trusts move HC to block chair’s casting vote at Tata Sons meet
points: Tata Trusts have launched a legal challenge against Tata Sons concerning the chairman's casting vote, citing governance issues before a crucial board meeting.
They argue that earlier resolutions breach the company’s articles and are seeking compensation.
Holding a significant stake in Tata Sons, the Trusts aim to ensure their nominee directors' votes carry equal weight, reflecting the continuing tensions over control in India's largest conglomerate.

items.title: Big, fat Bihar wedding makes global headlines
points: Mokama MLA Anant Singh's daughter Shivangi's wedding attracted attention due to its enormous scale and extravagant displays.
Over 400,000 guests were invited, with six helipads and a massive feast prepared by 500 cooks.
However, food distribution led to chaos as guests struggled to find plates amidst the crowd.
Animal welfare concerns arose from the event, particularly regarding horse racing and a captive elephant.

items.title: India playing leading role in global war on terror, says Amit Shah
points: Amit Shah, the Union home minister, reaffirmed India's unwavering dedication to fighting terrorism while honoring the memories of those affected by the 26/11 attacks.
He praised the bravery of both soldiers and innocent civilians, asserting that the Modi government’s unwavering stance against terrorism is garnering global recognition.
Shah also highlighted that united action is essential, as terrorism remains a grave threat to humanity.

items.title: Colombo Security Conclave reaffirms commitment to promote regional peace
points: The Maldives hosted the 8th NSA-level meeting of the Colombo Security Conclave, uniting member states in their shared goal of enhancing regional peace and security.
By emphasizing capacity-building and collaboration, the attendees laid out a roadmap for security cooperation through 2026-27, marking a commitment to address evolving challenges.
India reaffirmed its resolve to engage actively with CSC countries to foster stronger ties and collective security measures.

items.title: Mumbai police issue lookout circulars against CJP’s Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka, Saurav Das
points: CJP co-convener Saurav Das was barred from flying to London due to a lookout circular.
The Centre informed the Delhi high court that this action was taken at Mumbai police's request.
Saurav Das's passport is under scrutiny for several discrepancies regarding his identity.
His legal team argued that the travel ban infringes upon his fundamental rights.
The court proceedings continue as he prepares to respond to the notice issued.

items.title: Delhi high court nixes order to cancel NGO’s FCRA licence
points: In a pivotal decision, the Delhi High Court has ruled in favor of the Socio Legal Information Centre, restoring its FCRA licence that was previously annulled by the Home Ministry.
The court indicated that there was a lack of evidence to support accusations of the NGO's anti-government actions.
Moreover, the court deemed the assertions of the NGO negatively impacting India's image on the global stage as without merit.

items.title: Judicial member must on bench to confirm PMLA attachment, says Supreme Court
points: The Supreme Court has ruled that a judicial member must be present in the bench deciding asset attachments.
This decision focuses on ensuring legal objectivity in the proceedings related to the Prevention of Money Laundering Act.
The ruling addresses the competence of administrative members in handling questions of law and conflicting judgments.
The judgment is applicable prospectively and does not allow reopening of past decisions.

items.title: Bihar move illegal, says Supreme Court, quashes premature release of former MP Anand Mohan
points: In a significant ruling, the Supreme Court has annulled the Bihar government's controversial decision to release Anand Mohan, who was serving time for murder.
The state's attempt to modify prison regulations for his early exit was found unconstitutional.
Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu criticized the justification threshold for such a change, ultimately mandating that Anand Mohan must surrender within a month.

items.title: Supreme Court to banks: Give nod to try officials in 7 days
points: The Supreme Court has demanded that HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Sammaan Capital, and PNB Home Finance provide unconditional sanctions.
These sanctions involve officials implicated in collusion with builders in housing fraud schemes.
The banks' CMDs must articulate their non-compliance in court if not met within a week.
CBI’s investigations have led to chargesheets, and trials will commence once the necessary sanctions are secured, underscoring the urgency for timely judicial processes.

items.title: 7 months on, mediation in Sunjay Kapur case hits deadlock
points: Mediation efforts between Rani Kapur and Priya Sachdev Kapur over Sunjay Kapur's estate ended without resolution.
Former Chief Justice DY Chandrachud, who mediated the dispute, reported reaching an impasse.
Despite 15 sessions aimed at settlement, both parties did not show flexibility or understanding.
The Supreme Court noted that no settlement can be forced upon unwilling parties.
The court decided to close the mediation process and will issue a ruling soon.

items.title: Opposition worried, feels government won’t risk another defeat
points: The call for a Parliament session by the BJP to discuss the delimitation bill has taken the opposition by surprise.
As uncertainty looms, there are rising concerns among opposition parties about the potential impact on their voting power.
The DMK, having previously opposed similar measures, now adopts a cautious stance.
In contrast, Congress leaders maintain confidence, even as the government's influence grows.

items.title: Special Parliament session from November 30; women’s quota on agenda
points: Beginning November 30, the government is set to convene a brief session of Parliament focused on critical delimitation bills.
These proposed laws are designed to establish a women's quota in the Lok Sabha by 2029, boosting its membership to 850 seats.
Despite previous challenges in passing the bill, the government is optimistic about rallying support.

items.title: Supreme Court raps MNCs for ‘double standard’ on food quality
points: The Supreme Court addressed concerns regarding the quality of food products offered by multinational companies in India.
It emphasized the need for uniform standards across different countries to protect Indian consumers.
The court directed the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India to enforce strict labeling regulations.
Companies must not alter product compositions or conceal ingredient information.
This ruling aims to ensure consumer health and transparency in labeling practices.

items.title: Pension, insurance for 15 lakh gig workers likely by year-end
points: The government plans to announce a pension scheme and health insurance for gig workers soon.
Workers enrolled on the e-Shram portal will be the primary beneficiaries of these initiatives.
The National Social Security Board will discuss contributory models, including a 2% turnover-based contribution from platforms.
Trade unions have suggested immediate health and accident cover for these workers during onboarding.

items.title: No content from Pakistan to be shown in India, government reminds Netflix
points: In a move reflecting ongoing tensions, the Indian Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has urged Netflix to limit access to Pakistani content, particularly an upcoming series set to debut on December 4.
This action follows previous advisories related to national security concerns amid the India-Pakistan conflict.
Netflix has not clarified the series' availability in India, as industry groups pursue legal actions against Pakistani media.

items.title: Supreme Court sets timer for FSSAI, companies to implement warning labels
points: The Supreme Court has instructed the FSSAI to implement front-of-package labeling within four months.
Companies will have one year to comply with these regulations after the notification.
Labels will indicate high levels of sugar, saturated fat, and salt inside red hexagonal shapes to protect consumer health.
The court emphasized the importance of preventing public health crises associated with unhealthy food consumption.

items.title: Ex-terrorist fugitive’s 19-year run ends in arrest
points: Mohammad Mansha, a former terrorist, was arrested by a joint police team in Tral.
He had evaded law enforcement for nearly two decades since laying down arms in 2007.
Authorities revealed he was wanted in at least 13 criminal cases, including murder and conspiracy.
His criminal activities included the killing of a police officer back in 2000.
The operation involved meticulous planning and credible intelligence from various police units.

items.title: Sheshnag Lake row: Karan Singh questions need for wider road, PDP steps up heat
points: The ongoing debate about heavy machinery's presence near Sheshnag Lake along the Amarnath Yatra route is drawing intense scrutiny.
Karan Singh pointed out that not all pilgrimage paths necessitate vehicle accessibility for pilgrims.
Meanwhile, Mehbooba Mufti demanded transparency and public disclosure of any agreements linked to construction efforts.
The J&K government refuted claims about construction, insisting that machinery is operating at a considerable distance.

items.title: India-Germany submarine partnership can act as a catalyst for Indo-Pacific security: German envoy
points: Germany's commitment to technology transfer under the P-75I submarine project with India is being emphasized.
This partnership aims to enhance India's capabilities in undersea warfare technology, including Air-Independent Propulsion.
Both nations share mutual trust regarding the protection of sensitive technologies and strategic interests in the Indo-Pacific region.
The deal may also lead India to become a hub for submarine manufacturing for Southeast Asian nations.

items.title: Kashmir clerics split over Vande Mataram
points: A religious dispute over the national song Vande Mataram has intensified among clerics in Kashmir.
Sunni scholar Maulana Abdul Rashid Dawoodi urged for a fatwa regarding standing during its rendition.
Meanwhile, grand mufti Nasir-ul-Islam declared participation as impermissible under Islamic law.
Several clerics expressed regret after attending a function where Vande Mataram was played.
The controversy stems from a recent Union home ministry directive mandating its performance at official events.
